chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and learning the guitar
title: George Baquet's death and his father
summary: Visiting Baquet sick at home on his return from Chicago and at his wake; Old Man Baquet taught his sons clarinet.

blocks.x: Did you ever know of George's parents or any of the family?

Well, George, when I noticed, I went to his house on Roman, between right, on Roman, between Beville and Abbeville. Of course, I can't say Custom House because he was in Chicago. But I met his wife. And he come home from Chicago and I met his wife over there. There was about the 200 block of Bright Cross from, I don't know if you heard talk about this man, Gross, on Beville and Prayer. No, I don't think I know. Well, that's the way, that's the way he's at, Gross, Paul Gross. Mm-hmm. The Bible and Roman, I want to say, but George Barquet, when he come home sick, his sister was sick, his wife and his sister was living on Roman between Abbeville and Beville. Well, that's where he died at. See? Did you, you saw him after he came back from Chicago? Yeah, I seen him. I seen him, but he was sick. He was sick then. And that's where he died around there. I went to his house and seen him. Then I, when he died, well, I went to see him at the wake.
Do you remember, did his father play some instrument or was he in the band?

Old Man Barquet. Yeah, he used to play clarinet, Old Man Barquet. Old Man Barquet. If I'm mistaken, of course I was very young. I believe if I'm mistaken, I believe that's the one who taught George how to play and his brother. Of course you couldn't tell now, Achille Barquet and George Barquet, well, that's the old man who used to play clarinet too. Now, of course they used to have a band by the name of Alexander, but I ain't talking about that young fella now. He's paralyzed. He's got a stroke, I believe. But I'm talking about the old man.
I've seen his picture. He's playing off the horn right there.

That's right. He's dead now. And of course he used to play clarinet. He was a good musician. He used to be a director. He's almost like Chalini. I guess you were talking about Chalini. Of course I'm talking about them old timers like this fella here. Well, that's old time too. John Parker. Yes, I know him. John Parker? Willie. Willie Popper. Live off St. Philip's straight there. Well, I know him. Well, of course I can't mention the young fellas these days in time because they're coming up like they come from underneath the ground on me. Yeah. Because I don't know him. Of course I'm out of the picture, that's what I say. Of course it's like a fella get 50, 60, I hate him no more because he doesn't got too old.
